Theme

touch verb

also reach, lay a finger on, lay a finger on someone, sense of touch, feel (with the hands), feel one’s way, finger (handle), handle (with the hands)

classical

Traupman 396

tangō, tangere, tetigī, tāctum

verb, third conjugation

Useful for reaching far enough to touch a hold.

Other words

  • digitō attingere — lay a finger on

    attingō with digitō, ablative of means · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 4.6.1: atquī sī illam digitō attigerit, oculī illī īlicō ecfodientur (Lewis & Short), s.v. atquī; Traupman 102: aliquem ūnō digitō attingere; Traupman 338

  • tāctus, tāctūs m. — the sense of touch

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Quint. 1.4.20: corpus vīsū tāctūque manifestum (Lewis & Short s.v. vīsus); Traupman 59, 396

    Long ā by Lachmann’s law, from tangō.

  • temptō (tentō), temptāre, temptāvī, temptātum — feel (with the hands), handle

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 314

  • attrectō, attrectāre, attrectāvī, attrectātum — finger, handle

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 315

  • tractō, tractāre, tractāvī, tractātum — handle, touch, feel

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 325

Examples

  • Potesne illam ansam tangere?

    Can you touch that hold?composed

  • viam temptāre

    to feel one’s wayTraupman 314

  • cautē et cōgitātē rem tractāre

    to feel one’s way (figuratively)Traupman 314

See also grasp, reach, careful, don’t fall.
